title: Digital Literacy and Reading Habits of the Central University of Tamil Nadu Students: A Survey Study
extended_summary:
This paper examines the digital literacy skills and reading habits of students and research scholars at the Central University of Tamil Nadu in India. The authors ask how familiar respondents are with digital tools, how frequently they use digital environments and applications, and whether they prefer print or electronic reading formats. It is primarily a descriptive survey of current habits and self-perceived skills rather than an intervention study.

Data were collected with a structured questionnaire distributed through email, WhatsApp, and Telegram to 135 respondents drawn from undergraduate, postgraduate, integrated UG/PG, and research scholar groups. The survey covered self-ratings of typing, web search, computer, internet, and digital literacy skills; use of tools such as email, the web, databases, language apps, and video conferencing; and attitudes toward digital devices and digital literacy. The paper also asked about reading enjoyment, sources of reading recommendations, and format preferences for different reading situations.

The main conclusion is that respondents generally reported good digital literacy and comfort with digital tools, but they still preferred print books for many reading purposes, especially pleasurable reading and reading in bed or with children. Electronic formats were favored for quick access, travel, sharing, and maintaining large collections. The study argues that digital literacy is widespread among these university students, yet print remains the preferred medium for deeper or recreational reading. Because the study is self-report and descriptive, it does not test causal effects or compare literacy outcomes across subgroups beyond simple demographic descriptions.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI or chatbot system for producing and processing language-based outputs without a specific named product identified.
identified_tools.use_case: No generative AI tool was studied. The paper is a survey of university students' digital literacy, digital device use, and reading habits, including preferences for print versus electronic formats.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a cross-sectional survey study about digital literacy and reading habits, not an evaluation of an AI literacy intervention or AI tool. There is no comparison group, no moderator analysis, and no subgroup outcome analysis for emergent readers, multilingual learners, or students with disabilities.
impact_tier_rationale: No AI tool effect was measured, so there is no estimable impact on literacy outcomes. Reported results are descriptive self-reports only and do not support causal or subgroup effect claims.
